answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the load-bearing claim for switching: it records that the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply, onboarded quickly, and invoiced accurately. That directly supports the switch under the 18% spend mandate and the incumbent's refusal to reopen price. However, memory_c1 reminds us that renewal preserved integration stability with no migration work, and memory_c3 shows that a single-source posture created fragility. The assembly line running at 94% with no buffer means any delivery slip on switch-over would be costly. Therefore the switch is the right direction for TCO reduction, but I want to confirm the low-cost vendor's onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy from the archived source before committing, and I would structure the switch with a short parallel-run window if operationally feasible. If the archive contradicts memory_c2's favorable record, I would fall back to negotiate_terms with the incumbent, leveraging memory_c4's precedent that benchmarking at renewal moved the incumbent on price and payment terms, accepting that this may not fully close the 18% gap in one cycle.
